sentences.text: The skull of this sauropod was elongated and resembled the shape of Diplodocus.
Well-preserved skull fossils suggest that this sauropod may have possessed a beak-like keratinous sheath at the front of its snout.
The species Lavocatisaurus agrioensis was formally described in 2018, with an adult specimen designated as the holotype — the specimen the species is based on.
The genus name honors French paleontologist René Lavocat, and the species name refers to the Agrio del Medio locality where fossils were found.
Phylogenetic analysis classifies Lavocatisaurus as a basal member of the family Rebbachisauridae.
It is positioned as the sister group to Khebbashia, a clade comprising the subfamilies Rebbachisaurinae and Limaysaurinae.
This sauropod lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian stages) in the Rayoso Formation of northern Patagonia, Argentina.
Fossil evidence indicates a time range from 121.4 to 110.1 million years ago.
